title: Reducing Conversational Agents’ Overconfidence Through Linguistic Calibration
abstract: Abstract While improving neural dialogue agents’ factual accuracy is the object of much research, another important aspect of communication, less studied in the setting of neural dialogue, is transparency about ignorance. In this work, we analyze to what extent state-of-the-art chit-chat models are linguistically calibrated in the sense that their verbalized expression of doubt (or confidence) matches the likelihood that the model’s responses are factually incorrect (or correct). We find that these models are poorly calibrated, yet we show that likelihood of correctness can accurately be predicted. By incorporating such metacognitive features into the training of a controllable generation model, we obtain a dialogue agent with greatly improved linguistic calibration.

claims.text: State-of-the-art chit-chat models are poorly linguistically calibrated regarding their verbalized expressions of confidence versus factual accuracy.
The likelihood of correctness of chit-chat model responses can accurately be predicted using metacognitive features.
Incorporating metacognitive features into controllable generation model training improves the linguistic calibration of dialogue agents.

limitations.text: Transparency about ignorance and linguistic calibration in neural dialogue agents are less studied in existing research compared to factual accuracy.

methodologies.name: Metacognitive Controllable Generation Training
methodologies.description: Incorporates metacognitive accuracy-prediction features into the training of a controllable generation model to align verbalized confidence with factual likelihood.
